title: Generate the DealState sets the mock and marketWatch still hand-copy
body:
## Summary
Seven literal state lists in src/mock and lib/marketWatch stand for Rust rules that have no generated set: band-movable, open-table, quit-pending, seller-watch, order-expected.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/mock/backend.ts:297 and :1060 (band draft / band_set: PAIRING..AGREED), :564 and :1333 (group close / group open: PAIRING..NEGOTIATING), :946 (countersign: AGREED|APPROVED), apps/desktop/client/src/mock/forecast.ts:110 (quitPending, dispatcher.rs quit_summary), apps/desktop/client/src/lib/marketWatch.ts:30 (SELLER_OPEN, table-core market_watch_open seller arm), apps/desktop/client/src/mock/checks.ts:47 (ORDER_EXPECTED). bindings/dealStates.ts is generated from DealState predicates (crates/table-client/src/deal_states.rs) and pinned to the transition graph; these sets are not in it, so a Rust change leaves the mock answering differently with no test red. The exposure COMMITTED/PAID pair is already its own card (w1) and is not repeated here. Fixed: DealState predicates (or named consts) in table-core for each rule, rows in deal_states.rs SETS, regenerate, import in the client.

## Flow
- add the predicates in crates/table-core/src/deal.rs (and use them at the Rust call sites)
- add rows to crates/table-client/src/deal_states.rs; cargo run -p table-client --bin generate-bindings
- replace the 7 literals with the generated sets
- gates: cargo test -p table-core -p table-client; vitest src/mock src/lib/marketWatch.test.ts

## Expected impact
The browser preview and its tests move with Rust when a state rule changes. Touches table-core and the shared bindings surface, hence B.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition per state rule
Before: 7 hand-kept literal lists (grep of src/mock and lib/marketWatch.ts, comments excluded)
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - spans table-core, table-client, bindings (shared surfaces outside this round)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: table-client bindings test every_set_lists_exactly_the_states_its_predicate_keeps covers the new rows; seed: drop a state from one Rust predicate and watch vitest src/mock go red

title: The checklist's mandate line re-implements MandatePayload::check a second time
body:
## Summary
mock/checks.ts mandateFact judges the mandate clause by clause on its own, beside the mock check() in mock/simulate.ts; it skips category, max_deals_day, max_rounds and role (except rescue).

## Description
Rust composes the approval checklist mandate line from Wallet::mandate_check, the same MandatePayload::check the what-if and the owner accept use. The mock has two copies: apps/desktop/client/src/mock/simulate.ts:51 mockCheck (used by mandate_simulate, openTable and, since this round, owner accept) and apps/desktop/client/src/mock/checks.ts:63 mandateFact (the checklist). mandateFact has no category test (per_deal), no max_deals_day (velocity), no max_rounds or required-side test (band), and checks roles only for rescue. A deal outside its rules on any of those reads "Inside your rules" on the approval checklist in the preview while the what-if and the accept say refused. Fixed: mandateFact takes the mockCheck verdict (allow / ask / refuse clause+reason) and keeps only its wording (perDeal, threshold).

## Flow
- D-0193 with categories[D-0193] = compute: owner accept now false (built this round), checklist mandate line still pass
- fix: checksFor passes category, usage {dealsToday,totalToday} and rounds into mockChecks; mandateFact maps mockCheck to its four facts
- gates: vitest src/mock (checks.test pins the words)

## Expected impact
The preview checklist and the accept button agree. Could break: checks.test word pins on refused reasons (reason text comes from check()).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one mock of MandatePayload::check
Before: 2 implementations; 4 clause conditions present in mockCheck and absent in mandateFact (read of both files)
After: predicted 1 implementation
Method: simulation - read both; a grid instrument over the fixture deals is M and touches word pins
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/mock/checks.ts:77-91 per_deal without categories, band without max_rounds, velocity without max_deals_day
apps/desktop/client/src/mock/simulate.ts:78-104 the same clauses with them
instrument: vitest over every fixture deal with a category: the mandate line status (pass/fail) equals mockCheck(...).type !== refuse; red today on a category-refused deal

title: The mock's daily usage counts every day, Rust counts the agreement day
body:
## Summary
checksFor and ownerMandateAllows sum every agreed deal under the mandate ever; the ledger's usage_for counts only deals agreed on the probe deal's agreement day.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/src/repositories.rs:447 usage_for takes the UTC day of the deal's first AGREED audit row (else today) and counts deals agreed that day. apps/desktop/client/src/mock/backend.ts checksFor (spentTodayMinor) and ownerMandateAllows (usage) have no day at all (the mock keeps no agreement moment), so D-0187 (agreed earlier in the week, $212) counts against D-0193's $900 day. mandate_simulate approximates with created_at. Fixed: the fixtures record an agreed_at per deal (history 'agreed' steps or a field) and the three sites count by its UTC day.

## Flow
- open the preview mid-week: D-0193 usage 212 + 329 in the mock, 329 in Rust
- fix: MockDeal.agreedAt from buildHistory, a shared mock usageFor(deal, now)

## Expected impact
The preview daily-limit line and accept button stop refusing earlier than the wallet would. Fixture-wide change (fixtures.ts, scale.ts), hence B.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - mock usage matches usage_for
Before: D-0193 spent-today 541 (mock) vs 329 (Rust rule), walked on the fixture
After: predicted equal
Method: simulation - needs an agreement moment the fixtures do not carry
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-ledger/src/repositories.rs:458 "The day of the window: this deal's agreement day, else today."
apps/desktop/client/src/mock/backend.ts checksFor: "(the mock keeps no agreement day)"
instrument: vitest: a deal agreed yesterday under the same mandate does not count in checksFor / owner accept usage; red today

title: Mock emits settings:changed when the snapshot did not change
body:
## Summary
The mock sends settings:changed on every mandate_sign, pause/resume and settings write; Rust's 1 s tick publishes it only when the encoded snapshot differs.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:706-713 sends WalletEvent::Settings only when serde_json of settings() differs from the last one published. apps/desktop/client/src/mock/backend.ts emits settings:changed unconditionally in mandate_sign (first_run already false after the first set), pause_all_agents / resume_all_agents (already paused/resumed), tumbler_pin, settings_write, engine_select. UI reads that refresh on settings:changed (OwnerConfig, DealReview mandate_list) therefore refresh in the preview and its tests after a second mandate_sign, while the native shell sends nothing: the test that passes is a test that lies. Fixed: one mock publishSettings() that emits only when JSON.stringify(state.settings) changed.

## Flow
- mock: sign a second rule set -> settings:changed fires -> mandate_list re-read
- Rust: first_run already false -> no event -> mandate_list not re-read by that path

## Expected impact
Preview and tests stop relying on an event Rust does not send; may expose UI reads that need their own refresh (out of this context), hence B.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - mock event cadence matches Rust
Before: 10 unconditional emits; 2 of 2 mandate_sign calls emit (Rust: 1)
After: predicted 1 of 2
Method: simulation - the fix can turn src/windows tests red in other contexts; needs a worker that owns them
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:707-713 `published.settings.as_ref() != Some(&encoded)`
apps/desktop/client/src/mock/backend.ts mandate_sign: emit('settings:changed', state.settings) after first_run: false
instrument: vitest: listen on settings:changed, mandate_sign twice -> 1 event; then vitest src/windows to find reads that leaned on the extra event
